headline: Rangers put goalie James Reimer on waivers after just one start
take:
Per ESPN, the Rangers placed goalie James Reimer on waivers Thursday after just one start, and Daily Faceoff reports Sean Durzi is going on injured reserve. As Mollie Walker of the New York Post posted, Durzi is on IR "retroactive to Oct. 26," and Reimer "will still back up Dylan Garand tonight" ahead of Joonas Korpisalo's return.

Reimer's one start was rough. He has a .625 save percentage so far this season, and goals saved above expected, which measures how many goals a goalie stopped compared with what an average goalie would from the same shots, sits at -1.96. That's a tiny sample, but it matches his 14 games last season (-1.67), so the waiver move is hard to argue with. The Rangers (8-7-1) are being carried more by their goaltending (+1.2 goals saved above expected) than their finishing, which is 4.6 goals below expected.

Durzi's absence matters on the ice. He has played 19.79 minutes a game, and New York's share of expected goals, a measure of chance quality, drops 9.61 points when he plays. His 45 percent mark at five-on-five and two goals on 0.49 expected suggest some luck. We don't have a projection of who absorbs his minutes.
